Air quality, noise and weather from the citizen sensors of
[Sensor.Community](https://sensor.community) (formerly Luftdaten): your own
airRohr box, or the public sensors around your home.

> Developed without the hardware: feedback welcome. The integration was
> written and tested against recorded answers of the public API and of the
> airRohr firmware, not against a real box. Tell us on the Gladys forum how it
> behaves with yours.

This integration is not affiliated with Sensor.Community.

## What it does

- Reads **public sensors** of the Sensor.Community network by their id, with
  no account and no key.
- Reads **your own airRohr box** directly on your network, for live values
  every minute (optional).
- Creates **one device per sensor**: PM2.5, PM10, PM1 when measured,
  temperature, humidity, pressure, noise, CO2, depending on the sensor.
- Computes the **European Air Quality Index** (EEA) from PM2.5 and PM10, and
  tells how old the last measurement is: a silent sensor is flagged.
- Adds an **Air quality** dashboard widget, a scene trigger **Air quality
  changed** and a scene action **Get the air quality**.

Read only: the integration never changes anything on a sensor.

## Requirements

- Gladys Assistant **5.2.0** or later.
- Internet access for the public sensors (the Sensor.Community data API).
- For your own box: an airRohr (or any box running the Sensor.Community
  firmware) reachable from Gladys, with a **fixed IP address** (DHCP
  reservation on your router).
- For the nearby search: the location of your house, set in **Settings →
  Houses**. The integration asks for access to the house coordinates on the
  install screen; it only uses them for this search.

## Configuration

### Choose the sensors

1. Open the **Configuration** tab of the integration.
2. Click **Find sensors near a house**: pick the house (empty: the first
   house with a location) and a radius (empty: 2 km). The result lists the
   sensors that sent data in the last 5 minutes, nearest first, with their
   type, distance and measures, and the ids ready to copy.
3. Copy the ids you want into **Sensor ids**, separated by commas (20 at
   most). The id is also the number shown when you click a sensor on the
   [map](https://maps.sensor.community).
4. Save: the devices appear in the **Discovery** tab once their first
   measurement is read. Add them to Gladys.

Tip: a dust sensor (SDS011, SPS30…) and a weather sensor (BME280, DHT22…) of
the same box have two different ids: add both.

### Your own airRohr box

Enter its IP address in **Address of your airRohr box** (for example
`192.0.2.20`). Use the IP address: names ending in `.local` do not resolve
from the integration's container. The box is read every minute through its
`/data.json` page; no password is needed.

### Other settings

- **Refresh of the public sensors**: every 5, 10, 15 or 30 minutes. The public
  data moves every 5 minutes and Sensor.Community asks for moderation: 5
  minutes is the fastest.
- **Language**: the language of the feature names (set when a device is added)
  and of the texts sent to scenes. French by default.

The **Check the sensors** button reads every configured sensor and tells
what each one answers: its type and the age of its measurement, no data, or
an error.

## Devices

### Public sensor

One device per id, named `Sensor.Community #<id> (<type>)`. Its features
follow what the sensor measures:

| Feature                  | Unit  | Sensors                         |
| ------------------------ | ----- | ------------------------------- |
| PM2.5, PM10              | µg/m³ | SDS011, SPS30, PMS, HPM, NextPM |
| PM1                      | µg/m³ | SPS30, PMS, NextPM              |
| Temperature, Humidity    | °C, % | BME280, DHT22, SHT3x, HTU21D    |
| Pressure                 | hPa   | BME280, BMP280, BMP180          |
| Sea-level pressure       | hPa   | BME280, BMP280, BMP180          |
| Noise (LAeq), min, max   | dB    | DNMS                            |
| CO2                      | ppm   | SCD30                           |
| Air quality index (EAQI) | 1–6   | every particle sensor           |
| Measurement age          | min   | every sensor                    |

Each value is the mean of the measurements of the last 5 minutes, like the
Sensor.Community map. PM1 is shown as a PM2.5-type feature (Gladys has no PM1
category), named "PM1".

### Your airRohr box

One device named `airRohr <chip id>` (for example `airRohr esp8266-1234567`),
with every sensor plugged into the box. The name of each feature carries the
sensor: "Temperature (BME280)", "Temperature (DHT22)".

### Air quality index

The **European Air Quality Index** of the European Environment Agency, from 1
to 6: good, fair, moderate, poor, very poor, extremely poor. The worst of
PM2.5 and PM10 sets the level (bands revised in 2024: PM2.5 up to 5, 15, 50,
90, 140 µg/m³; PM10 up to 15, 45, 120, 195, 270 µg/m³). The EEA computes it
on validated means of reference stations: on a low-cost sensor and 5
minutes, it is an indication.

### Measurement age

Minutes since the last measurement of the sensor. Past 15 minutes the
measurement is **stale**: the integration stops sending its values (Gladys
keeps showing the last ones with their date), the widget says "Stale" and the
age keeps growing, so a scene can warn you.

## Widget

Add the **Air quality** widget to a dashboard.

- With a **sensor** chosen in its settings: live tiles (PM2.5, PM10,
  temperature, humidity), the level of the European index colored by its band
  (green for good and fair, orange for moderate, red beyond) and the age of the
  measurement.
- Without a sensor: one row per sensor measuring particles, with its level.

## Scenes

### Trigger: Air quality changed

Starts the scene when the European index of a sensor reaches another level,
confirmed by two readings in a row (one puff of smoke does not fire it).
Filters: the sensor, and the new levels that matter (for example poor, very
poor, extremely poor). Variables available to the following actions: sensor
name, level (as a word in the configured language), level 1 to 6, previous
level, pollutant setting the level, PM2.5 and PM10.

### Action: Get the air quality

Gives the air quality of one sensor, or, without a sensor, the worst of the
sensors measured in the last 15 minutes. Outputs: a **summary** ready for a
notification ("Poor · PM2.5 62 µg/m³ · PM10 80 µg/m³ · 3 min ago"), the
level as a word, its key and number, PM2.5, PM10 and the measurement age.

## Scene examples

- **Close the windows when the air gets bad**: trigger "Air quality changed"
  with the levels poor, very poor, extremely poor → send a message "Air is
  \{\{triggerEvent.data.level_label\}\} around \{\{triggerEvent.data.sensor_name\}\}: close the windows".
- **Morning briefing**: at 7:30 → action "Get the air quality" → send the
  summary in the morning message.
- **Silent sensor**: trigger on the "Measurement age" feature above 60 minutes
  → notify that the sensor (or your box's Wi-Fi) is down.
- **Ventilation**: when the index of your own box goes back to good or fair,
  start the controlled mechanical ventilation.

## Troubleshooting

- **No device in the Discovery tab**: a sensor appears once its first
  measurement is read. Click **Check the sensors**: "no data in the last 5
  minutes" means the sensor is offline, or the id is wrong (the API answers
  the same for both). Check the id on the map.
- **The status says the API does not answer**: the Sensor.Community API is
  down or unreachable from Gladys; the readings resume on their own.
- **Your box does not answer**: check its IP address (a fixed one), that it
  is powered and on the same network as Gladys, and open
  `http://<its address>/data.json` in a browser.
- **A box with an old firmware** (before 2020) has no `/metrics` page: its
  device is then named after its address, and a new address makes a new
  device. Update the firmware.
- Logs: open the integration logs from Gladys. Set `LOG_LEVEL=debug` to see
  every reading.

## Limits

- Data of citizen sensors, not of reference stations: low-cost dust sensors
  over-read in humid air (fog, rain). Use the values as trends.
- Public sensors are read every 5 minutes at most, and at most 20 sensors.
- Only PM2.5 and PM10 feed the European index: the other pollutants of the
  official index (ozone, NO2, SO2) are not measured by these sensors.
- PM4 and particle counts (SPS30, IPS-7100) are not shown: Gladys has no
  category for them.
- The integration reads; it never configures a box.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Sensor.Community asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Citizen sensors | `section` | No | Read public Sensor.Community sensors (no account) by their id, the number shown on the map, or your own airRohr box on your network. Not affiliated with Sensor.Community. |
| Sensor ids | `string` | No | The ids of the public sensors to read, separated by commas (20 at most). The "Find sensors near a house" button below lists those around you. |
| Address of your airRohr box | `string` | No | Optional: the IP address of your own box on your network, read every minute for live values. Use its IP address: names ending in .local do not resolve from the integration. |
| Refresh of the public sensors | `select` | No | The public data moves every 5 minutes, and Sensor.Community asks for moderation: 5 minutes is the fastest. |
| Language | `select` | No | Language of the feature names (set when a device is added) and of the scene texts. |

## How to install Sensor.Community in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Sensor.Community appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-sensor-community:1.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-sensor-community](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-sensor-community).

Sensor.Community requires Gladys `>=5.2.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Sensor.Community is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core.
